title: ArcadeHub Mobile
premise: A neon-styled mobile arcade hub that wraps three quick-play mini-games inside a faux social gaming app interface.
interaction_model: Touch-first tab navigation and one-thumb arcade controls, with taps for menu actions, jumping, reaction timing, and side-based movement.
objective: Browse the arcade lobby and launch short score-chasing challenges, especially the featured runner, to survive longer and earn higher scores.
progression: Session-based progression with immediate retries, rising speed or pressure within each mini-game, and light meta flavor through XP, coins, profile stats, and social UI dressing rather than deep persistence.
mood: Playful, energetic, colorful, snackable, and lightly competitive.
likely_audience: younger players who enjoy bright social-game presentation
players who like quick reflex challenges
confidence_notes: High confidence that the codebase is a mobile arcade hub with a featured endless-runner-style game and two supporting microgames.
Moderate confidence on whether the intended identity should be treated as one game or a mini-game collection, because the shell brands everything as one app experience.
High confidence that the recreation should preserve the social-lobby wrapper, canvas overlay, and short-session replay loop.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-first HTML5 arcade app called ArcadeHub Mobile that feels like a neon social gaming lobby with four bottom tabs: Home, Profile, Crew messages, and Settings. The Home screen should feature a large banner for a flagship game called Sky Sprint, plus two quick-challenge cards named Snack Catch and Signal Duel. When the player taps a game card, open a full-screen canvas gameplay overlay with a compact HUD, a score display labeled as XP, a tap-to-start hint, an exit button, and a game-over modal with retry and main menu buttons. The flagship gameplay should be a one-thumb endless runner/platformer where a small mascot automatically advances across moving floating platforms, gravity pulls the character downward, the player taps to jump only while grounded, coins can be collected for points, the scrolling speed slowly increases, and falling off the screen ends the run. Include a second mini-game where a chef avatar moves left or right depending on which side of the screen is touched, catching falling pizzas for points while avoiding bombs that cause instant failure. Include a third mini-game built around reaction timing: the screen tells the player to wait, then flashes a clear signal like TAP NOW, and the player must tap only after the cue but before a short timer expires; tapping early or too late causes a loss, while successful reactions add to score and repeat the duel with faster pacing. Wrap all of this in a glossy sci-fi mobile UI with dark purple panels, cyan and violet accents, playful social details like friend avatars, a mock chat thread, profile stats, coin counters, toggleable music and sound effects, small success and failure reaction animations, and responsive touch-friendly presentation for portrait phones. Keep the tone bright, arcade-like, and instantly replayable rather than progression-heavy.
